page.layout: One column of running text, with a centred heading block (CONCIO XXXV., Eccles. 19.) before the second passage. The woodcut ornament stands at the start of the first sentence of that passage. No marginal notes. Running head at top, page number at top left.

main_text.l: Legitur de Zenone Cittieo, quòd ipse simul
At ille quum sentiret affectum amoris, furre-
xit. Hoc admirante Cleanthe, etiam à bonis,
xit se vir integerrimus imminenti periculo.
Filius castissimæ virginis, autorque vitæ ac
corda nostra, & auertat oculos nostros, ne
stras, vt cernant veritatem, quæ nos verè
liberos reddat, & in nobis regem, vinum, &
1 Duo grauissimi morbi iam passim gras-
santur, quos sanare vult Sapiens his verbis.

page.notes: The woodcut ornament at the start of the italic passage is not text. The hyphen after "suppli" is printed as a dot at the line end and is copied as a hyphen. "Eccles. 19." is set apart on its own line and treated as a verse reference. Otherwise the text is clear; no doubtful readings.
